bullets.title: NVDA: Vera Rubin on track; H200 shipments to China begin; AI factory capex scaling to $100B+
bullets.body: NVIDIA CEO Huang confirmed Vera Rubin GPU is on schedule and already in production. Separately, a senior U.S. official confirmed H200 AI chip shipments to China have commenced. Morgan Stanley pegs 1 GW GB200/GB300/Vera Rubin buildout at $35–49B, with Jensen Huang suggesting next-gen AI factories could approach $100B per GW—roughly double current estimates.

bullets.title: TSMC Q2 Thursday: +59% net profit, >68% gross margin expected; 2nm ramp with Google Pixel 11
bullets.body: TSMC reports Q2 on July 16 with consensus expecting NT$1.27T revenue, net profit up 59% YoY to NT$632.6B (US$19.6B), and gross margin exceeding 68%—the 10th consecutive quarter of profit growth. Samsung is mounting a 2nm counteroffensive. Separately, TSMC revenue reportedly surged 36% with Google Pixel 11 allegedly leading 2nm ramp adoption.

bullets.title: MU hits $1.1T market cap; SLC NAND seen surging 120-170% in H2 2026; bullish options flow
bullets.body: Micron's market cap closed above $1.1 trillion, surpassing Berkshire Hathaway. SLC NAND is forecast to rise 120–170% in H2 2026 per Trendforce, with MU holding a 21% share. One trader flagged MU order flow as 'incredibly BULLISH all day,' and noted a head-and-shoulders undercut as a potential short-squeeze setup for the broader semiconductor sector.

bullets.title: ORCL: FCF hits historic low; stock at 52-week lows, down 62% from peak
bullets.body: Oracle's free cash flow has plummeted to the lowest level in company history. ORCL has fallen 62% from its September 2025 all-time high, erasing over $500 billion in market cap. The stock hit new 52-week lows intraday; Tradr is launching a 2X Short ORCL Daily ETF (ORCZ) on July 15. Separately, FT reports Oracle is the lead contender to provide top-secret cloud services to Japan's government.

bullets.title: META: Q2 earnings July 29; 5GW Louisiana data center prioritizes grid over silicon; AI price war favors well-capitalized players
bullets.body: Meta confirmed Q2 earnings after close July 29. A tech infrastructure thread highlighted Meta's 5GW Louisiana campus as prioritizing grid power access over chip availability as the primary AI compute constraint. Separately, an analyst initiated deeper META coverage with an AI-to-ARPU model, positioning it as an ads company building a token factory alongside potential compute/API revenue.

bullets.title: Data center buildout faces mounting headwinds: $286B canceled/delayed, PJM 7GW shortfall, NY moratorium
bullets.body: An estimated $156B in data center projects were canceled or delayed in 2025, with another $130B in Q1 2026 amid community pushback and new moratoriums. PJM failed to secure 7GW needed for 2028 grid stability; without price caps, electricity would clear 70% higher at ~$555/MWh. New York became the first state to impose a one-year ban on new hyperscale data centers (≥50MW), and state-level moratorium bills are spreading. For the first time, a majority of Americans oppose building more data centers.

bullets.title: SEMI raises 2026 equipment forecast to $165.9B (+23%); semiconductor stocks hit 20% of S&P 500
bullets.body: SEMI raised its global semiconductor equipment sales forecast to $165.9B for 2026, up 23.2% YoY and well above its prior estimate of $145B, citing strong AI-driven demand for leading-edge logic, memory, and advanced packaging. Separately, semiconductor stocks now account for 20% of the S&P 500 weighting—an all-time high.

bullets.title: VIAV flagged as testing-sector play similar to AEHR; silicon photonics burn-in entering high-volume production
bullets.body: A fintwit account recommended VIAV as a similar play to AEHR in the testing process, noting 'different part of the testing process' but positive on current levels. Separately, silicon photonics burn-in has moved from qualification to automated high-volume production, a bullish signal for optical interconnect supply chain names AVGO, LITE, and COHR.

bullets.title: SNDK and MU seen as HBF beneficiaries; HBM4 timing and silicon photonics ramp discussed
bullets.body: One account suspects High Bandwidth Fabric (HBF) is being deployed for generative AI data centers, with AEHR validating the technology with customers on its second earnings call—implying SNDK and MU as key beneficiaries. The broader GAI infrastructure trade (NVDA, MU, SNDK, LITE) described as a structural winner regardless of market volatility.

bullets.title: TSEM planning $3B Japan expansion for silicon photonics and advanced packaging
bullets.body: TSEM is planning a $3B expansion in Japan focused on 300mm silicon photonics capacity, silicon germanium, and advanced packaging—directly aligned with AI interconnect demand.

bullets.title: Intel Foundry secures AMD, NVIDIA, OpenAI design wins on 18A/14A; EMIB yields hit 98%
bullets.body: Intel Foundry booked design wins from AMD, NVIDIA, and OpenAI on its 18A and 14A process nodes. EMIB (embedded multi-die interconnect bridge) technology has reached 98% yields, a meaningful milestone for advanced packaging credibility.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Android settlement with Epic allows third-party app stores; MediaTek wins Pixel 11 5G modem over Qualcomm
bullets.body: Google and Epic settled their dispute, with third-party Android app stores launching the following week—a significant change to Android's app distribution model. Separately, Google selected MediaTek over Qualcomm and Samsung for 5G modem chips in the upcoming Pixel 11, per supply chain sources, as MediaTek expands its standalone modem footprint.

bullets.title: BofA sell signal triggered as fund managers at most long since December 2024; cash at 3.6%
bullets.body: Bank of America warns a stock market sell signal has been triggered after fund manager cash levels fell to 3.6%, one of the lowest levels this century. Separately, fund managers are now the most long stocks since December 2024, and the top 10 S&P 500 stocks make up 43% of total index weight—approaching historical concentration peaks.

bullets.title: China Q2 GDP misses at 4.3% YoY, slowest since 2022; mixed data with industrial output beat
bullets.body: China's Q2 GDP grew 4.3% YoY, missing the 4.5% consensus and well below 5% prior—the slowest pace since 2022. June industrial production beat at 5.3% YoY vs 4.6% estimate, and retail sales turned positive at +1.0% vs -0.1% estimate. Fixed investment fell 5.7% YTD, worse than expected. DeepSeek reportedly planning IPO as early as Q2 2025 and raised $7.4B, with ARR approaching $500M.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler bond spreads at record wides; Morgan Stanley projects $4–8T capex through 2028
bullets.body: Hyperscaler bond basket spreads widened to record levels, signaling credit stress in mega-cap tech. Morgan Stanley projects 80GW of new compute capacity by 2028 requiring $4–8T in capex funded via debt and equity issuance, with free cash flow expected to turn negative during this period.

bullets.title: Soft June CPI drives rate-hike odds below 17%; headline CPI posts one of largest MoM drops in 80 years
bullets.body: July Fed rate hike odds collapsed from over 40% to under 17% in a single day following the June CPI print. The headline CPI monthly decline was among only the 21st occurrence in 80 years of a ≥0.4% MoM drop. The euro rallied above 1.1400 and Asian stocks surged—KOSPI +6%, SK Hynix +10%—on the data.

bullets.title: VST, CEG, TLN: PJM capacity auction shortfall seen as structural positive for merchant power
bullets.body: A fintwit account notes the PJM 2028/2029 capacity auction shows a massive shortfall, arguing merchant power names CEG, VST, and TLN should trade up on the tight capacity outlook—though the author flags 18 months of being wrong on similar setups. Talen Energy cleared 10,180 MW at $325/MW-day, implying ~$1.2B gross capacity revenue for the 2028/2029 planning year.

bullets.title: GEV: New gas turbine orders blocked until 2030, structural demand tailwind
bullets.body: A fintwit account flagged that new gas turbine deliveries are unavailable until 2030, a structural demand tailwind for GEV as power infrastructure investment accelerates.

bullets.title: AMZN deploys novel RNG network topology for data center infrastructure, claiming 45% cost savings
bullets.body: Amazon unveiled 'Resilient Network Graphs' (RNG) topology for its data center network, based on random graphs rather than traditional fat-tree architecture. The company developed a custom routing protocol (Spraypoint) and claims up to 45% cost savings vs fat-tree networks at similar oversubscription ratios. Amazon has deployed two versions of RNG to date.

bullets.title: AAPL: Jony Ive design work criticized; iPhone builds seen slowing in 2027; 20% global smartphone share
bullets.body: Apple reached 20% global smartphone market share, but a new supply chain report warns iPhone builds are expected to slow in 2027 amid price increases and weak US upgrade cycles. Jony Ive's recent design output was publicly criticized by a verified tech commenter. Separately, OpenAI dismissed Apple's lawsuit alleging trade secret violations related to its home speaker product.
